Parallel Relay Annealed SMC

Technique

We conceive of each SMC round as analogous to path sampling where our normalising constant estimator can be decomposed into several independent local estimators (which can then be estimated in parallel):

\[ \hat{\Bigg(\frac{Z_1}{Z_0}\Bigg)} = \hat{\Bigg(\frac{Z_{\alpha_2}}{Z_0}\Bigg)} \cdot \hat{\Bigg(\frac{Z_{\alpha_3}}{Z_{\alpha_2}}\Bigg)} \dots \hat{\Bigg(\frac{Z_{\alpha_{J}}}{Z_{\alpha_{J-1}}}\Bigg)}\cdot \hat{\Bigg(\frac{Z_1}{Z_{\alpha_{J}}} \Bigg) }\]

For the \(j\)-th local estimator \(\hat{\Big(\frac{Z_{\alpha_{j+1}}}{Z_{\alpha_{j}}}\Big)}\), we only require the ability to sample from the distribution of \(\alpha_{j}\). Once we have a sample from \(\alpha_{j}\), we can take annealing steps towards \(\alpha_{j+1}\) according to a temperature schedule and compute:

\[ \hat{\Big(\frac{Z_{\alpha_{j}}}{Z_{\alpha_{j-1}}}\Big)} = \prod_{k: \beta_k \in \mathcal C_j} \Big( \frac{1}{N_j} \sum_{i =1}^{N_j} w_{i,j,k} \Big)\]

where \(\mathcal C_j\) is the set of all temperatures at which resampling occurred.

This is all possible in vanilla annealed SMC too: but the way to generate samples from each \(\alpha_j\) is to get there sequentially, starting from our reference distribution \(\eta\) (with \(\alpha_2, \dots \alpha_{J}\) along the way). This is unavoidable if we run a single round of SMC.

However, if we run multiple SMC rounds, we can choose a temperature where resampling occurred in previous rounds as our \(\alpha_j\) for our next round- since we have a sample from its distribution already available. If we do so, we circumvent the requirement to sample and compute our sub-estimates sequentially, and can efficiently parallelise the computation of the normalising constant ratio.

Definitions

Relay

We define the \(j\)-th relay as the \(j\)-th such “sub-round” of annealed SMC sampling starting from \(\alpha_{j}\), going through an annealed path \(\mathcal B_j = \{\alpha_{j} = \beta_{j, 0} < \beta_{j, 1} \dots \beta_{j, T_j -1} < \beta_{j, T_j} = \alpha_{j+1}\}\) ending at \(\alpha_{j+1}\).

Checkpoint temperature

A checkpoint temperature is one where resampling has occurred and thus we have a set of samples from its true distribution. We can call the corresponding set of samples a checkpoint set.

Relay temperature

The starting temperature of each relay is a relay temperature. Each relay temperature is also a checkpoint temperature.

In order to choose our set of relay temperatures \(\mathcal A = \{0 = \alpha_1 <\alpha_2 \dots < \alpha_{J} < \alpha_{J+1} = 1\}\)’s from the pool of checkpoint temperatures, we need to ensure that:

  • the number of relays \(J\) is enough to utilise all available parallel computing resources
  • the number of intermediate annealing steps \(T_j\) is approximately uniform across relays
  • it is “close” to the optimal set of annealing temperatures
  • we don’t repeatedly use the same checkpoints
  • maintaining composability/comparability of local estimators (by choosing checkpoints from same round)

Notation

Symbol Description
\(Z_{\beta}\) the normalising constant \(\int \pi_\beta(x) dx\) for our unnormalised annealing probability density at temperature \(\beta\)
\(\hat Z_{\alpha \rightarrow \beta}\) our estimator for the ratio of normalising constants \(\frac{Z_{\beta}}{Z_\alpha}\)
\(R\) Number of rounds of SMC
\(J^{(r)}\) Number of relays in the \(r\)-th round
\(X^{(r)}_{i,j,k}\) Particle \(i\) of the \(k\)-th annealing step of the \(j\)-th relay of the \(r\)-th round
\(w^{(r)}_{i,j,k}\) Weight associated with particle \(X^{(r)}_{i,j,k}\)
\(\mathbb X^{(r)}_{j,k}\) The particle set of the \(k\)-th annealing step of the \(j\)-th relay of the \(r\)-th round
\(\mathbb Y^{(s)}_{\alpha}\) Checkpoint set at temperature \(\alpha \in \mathcal C^{(r)}\) from the \(s\)-th round (\(s< r\))
\(\mathcal A^{(r)}\) Sorted set of relay temperatures for round \(r\)
\(\mathcal B^{(r)}\) Sorted optimal global schedule for round \(r\)
\(\mathcal B^{(r)}_j\) Sorted local schedule for \(j\)-th relay of round \(r\)
\(\mathcal C^{(r)}_j\) Sorted set of checkpoint temperatures encountered in the \(j\)-th relay of round \(r\)
\(\mathcal C^{(r)} = \cup_{j=1}^{J^{(r)}} C^{(r)}_j\) Sorted set of checkpoint temperatures in round \(r\)
\(\mathcal H^{(r)} = \cup_{s =1}^{r-1} C^{(s)}\) Sorted set of checkpoint temperatures until round \(r\)
\(G\) Number of cores available
\(N_j^{(r)}\) Number of particles in the \(j\)-th relay of the \(r\)-th round (for now we can assume all relays have same number of particles \(N^{(r)}\))
\(T_j^{(r)} = |\mathcal B_j^{(r)}| - 1\) Number of annealing steps in the \(j\)-th relay of round \(r\)

Algorithm

For SMC round \(r \in \{1, 2, \dots R\}\) with optimal temperature schedule \(\mathcal B^{(r)}\):

  1. Choose the set of relay temperatures \(\mathcal A^{(r)} = RelayTemps(\mathcal B^{(r)}, \mathcal H^{(r)}, G)\)

  2. For relay \(j\) in \(\{1, 2, \dots J^{(r)}\}\):

    1. Initialise particle set \(\mathbb X^{(r)}_{j,0} = Resample(\mathbb Y_{\alpha_j}, N^{(r)}_j)\).
    2. Set local schedule \(\mathcal B^{(r)}_j =\{\alpha_j\} \cup \{\beta \in \mathcal B^{(r)}: \alpha_{j} \leq \beta \leq \alpha_{j+1}\} \cup \{\alpha_{j+1}\}\).
    3. Run \(SMCSampler( \mathbb X^{(r)}_{j,0 } , \mathcal B_{j}^{(r)})\).
    4. Compute local estimator \(\hat Z_{\alpha_j \rightarrow \alpha_{j+1}} = \prod_{k: \beta_k \in \mathcal C^{(r)}_j} \Big( \frac{1}{N_j} \sum_{i =1}^{N_j} w^{(r)}_{i,j,k} \Big)\) (in practice iteratively update after each resampling during SMC sampling)

  3. Compute global estimator \(\hat Z_{0\rightarrow 1}^{(r)} = \prod_{j = 1}^{J^{(r)}} \hat Z_{\alpha_j \rightarrow \alpha_{j+1}}\)
